hints: Focus on what lithium aluminium hydride does to a carboxylic acid functional group.
Notice the starting molecule has two $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ groups joined together, so apply that change to both ends.
Count the carbons to check nothing is lost, then decide what a $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ becomes when fully reduced to a primary alcohol group.
walkthrough:
**Recall the power of LiAlH4**

Great start, let's remember our reducing agents. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a very strong reducing agent and it reduces carboxylic acids all the way to primary alcohols.

General change:
$$\text{R-CO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Look at our starting acid**

Now look closely at ethanedioic acid. Its structure is $\text{HO}_2\text{C-CO}_2\text{H}$, which is two carboxylic acid groups joined directly together.

We can write it as:
$$\text{HOOC-COOH}$$

**Reduce both ends**

Because we use an excess of $\text{LiAlH}_4$, both $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ groups are fully reduced. Each $\text{-COOH}$ becomes a $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group.

Overall change:
$$\text{HOOC-COOH} \rightarrow \text{HOCH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Name the product**

The product $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ has two carbons and an $\text{-OH}$ on each carbon. That is ethane-1,2-diol, a diol with the carbon skeleton unchanged.

options.A: Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, has only one $\text{-OH}$ group and would come from ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. Here we start with a dicarboxylic acid with two carbons, and both carbons and both functional groups are retained, so we must get a diol, not a mono-alcohol.
options.B: Correct and well done. Each $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ group is reduced by excess $\text{LiAlH}_4$ to a primary alcohol $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$. So $\text{HOOC-COOH}$ gives $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which is ethane-1,2-diol. The two-carbon skeleton is unchanged.
options.C: Ethanedial, $\text{OHC-CHO}$, contains two aldehyde groups and is only a partial reduction product. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ in excess is too strong to stop at the aldehyde stage, it carries the reduction all the way to the primary alcohol.
options.D: Methane, $\text{CH}_4$, would require breaking the C-C bond and losing the oxygen atoms completely. Reduction with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ changes the functional groups but does not cleave the carbon skeleton, so both carbons remain in the product.
